groups.decision: MCP capability and transport descriptions are source-scoped; executable, database, filesystem and API capabilities require separate permission and isolation decisions.

Language examples differ in startup, cleanup, schema and permission-handler configuration. Python approve_all is not user approval; omitted handlers in other examples do not establish permission success. Literal Bearer ${TOKEN} strings do not demonstrate credential interpolation.

disabledMcpServers uses exact names on each create/resume request without changing global configuration. Creation/cold resume prevent startup and authentication; resident resume cannot undo already-spawned servers. Tool filtering and process suppression are different controls.

Wildcard, named-list and empty-list tool filtering have distinct semantics. No separate allow/disallow list is specified. These source capabilities are not authority to remove required project capabilities or grant dangerous tools.

Filesystem quick start uses npx automatic acquisition and an example /tmp scope. Printed session/response output is illustrative, not observed. Linked packages and server repositories are not reviewed merely by reference.

Local command/args and remote type/url are required, while headers/tools/timeouts are optional in these source tables. Defaults, millisecond units and credential routing require version-specific validation; optional configuration is not authenticated effective enforcement.

Diagnose startup, stderr, tool selection, remote accessibility, authentication and timeout/prompt failures independently. A running server, accessible URL or successful discovery cannot alone prove safe authorized execution; linked guides remain separately scoped.
